title: Add cohort stability index and alert weave for long-tail token variance
author: Evan Patel
description: Context: Long-tail spikes in per-request token cost and tail latency have been producing noisy alerts that are hard to triage. Root cause analysis shows that the noise frequently correlates with small, coherent cohorts (prompt shapes, tenant routing, or certain model variants) that briefly diverge. Motivation: introduce an explicit cohort-level stability signal that (1) surfaces which cohorts are driving long-tail variance, (2) powers an alert-weave that groups and suppresses short-lived noise, and (3) enables prioritized sampling for post-incident trace capture. This PR implements: - Cohort Stability Index (CSI): a bounded [0..1] score computed per cohort/window that combines normalized token-cost variance, tail-latency skew, and recent alert frequency. CSI is computed in the metrics service as a rolling sketch to control memory and cardinality. - Alert Weave: a policy layer that uses CSI to group alerts and apply short-circuit suppression for cohorts with transient instability (CSI spikes under configured duration), while still escalating sustained cohort regressions. - Dashboard + Heatmap: new 'Cohort Stability' dashboard that shows CSI sparklines, cohort membership counts, and a token-cost delta heatmap for quick root-cause triangulation. - Sampler seeding: when CSI crosses threshold, we increase sampled trace rate for affected cohorts via the sampling controller to capture KV cache state, kernel queue traces, and request headers. Implementation notes: - Metrics path: services/observability/metrics/cohort_index.go implements a compact bfloat sketch followed by a dampening window to avoid flapping. CSI tags: model_variant, route, tenant_id (tenant_id is optional and high-cardinality guarded by a cardinality cap). - Alerting path: services/alerting/policies/weave_policy.go implements grouping keys and suppression windows; default policy is non-breaking and opt-in per alertrule. - Dashboard: dashboards/cohort-stability.json includes preconfigured queries and example cohort selectors. - Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive. The default behavior preserves existing alerting; customers must opt-in to enable cohort-aware suppression via feature flag. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated rollout for internal telemetry team; 2) Monitor false-negative risk with an internal runbook; 3) Expand opt-in to selected tenants; 4) Gradual on-by-default if no regression. Checklist: - [x] Core CSI computation implemented and unit-tested - [x] Alert weave policy AND feature flag - [x] Dashboard and runbook - [x] Sampling integration (seeded) - [x] Docs added (observability/cohort-stability.md) - [x] E2E smoke in staging Tests: unit + integration; synthetic workload in perf-lab to validate non-flapping behavior. Related: ENG-3245 (reduce alert churn), ENG-3310 (prefetch sampling improvements).

release_notes: Introduce Cohort Stability Index (CSI) metric and opt-in Alert Weave policy. CSI helps cluster long-tail token-cost and latency variance by cohort, reduces alert noise via transient suppression, and seeds higher sampling rates for affected cohorts. Feature is gated; enable via helm values.featureFlags.cohortStability=true. No breaking changes.
notes_for_oncall: If alert volume drops after enabling Alert Weave, check the cohort_stability.eviction_rate and suppressed_alerts.time_series. Fallback toggle: disable feature flag to revert to legacy alerting. Run the provided synthetic spike job in perf-lab to validate sampling if traces are missing.
